subject: general
question: Kailash Satyarthi has received the Noble Prize in the field of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Peace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Kailash Satyarthi 

 
 
• Kailash Satyarthi is an Indian social activist who works and campaigned against child labour in India and elsewhere and advocated the right to education. 
 
• In 2014 he was the recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize, along with Pakistan Malala Yousafzai,** “for their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education”.**
 
• Kailash Satyarthi founded the movement called Bachapan Bachao Andolan in India. Hence statement B is correct. 
 
• Kailash Satyarthi is the fifth Indian Nobel prize winner. 
 
 

 
• Other Noble Prize winners from India:__

 __
 
• Rabindranath Tagore
 
• Chandrashekhar Venkataraman 
 
• Mother Teresa 
 
• Amartya Sen
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The*** 2025 Nobel Prizes ***were awarded across five categories, highlighting achievements in quantum physics, materials science, immunology, literature, and peace.

 
 
• **Physics Prize:**

 
 
• Awarded to** John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis** for their work in **macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits**, showcasing quantum mechanics at a macroscopic scale.
 
• Their work enabled advances in quantum computing, cryptography, and quantum sensors.
 
 
 
• **Chemistry Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to** Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar M. Yaghi** for their development of **metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), materials with vast internal surface areas** for various applications such as water harvesting, carbon capture, and toxic gas storage.
 
 
 
• **Medicine Prize**:
 
 
• Awarded to **Mary E. Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi **for **discovering regulatory T cells (Tregs) that prevent autoimmune diseases** and play a role in cancer therapy.
 
• Their work has revolutionized the understanding of autoimmune diseases and immunotherapy.
 
 
 
• **Literature Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to L**ászló Krasznahorkai **for his** visionary works, including "Satantango**", which explore themes of apocalyptic terror, chaos, and human isolation.
 
• Known for long, complex sentences and dark, philosophical narratives.
 
 
 
• **Peace Prize:**
 
 
• Awarded to **Maria Corina Machado**, a** Venezuelan leader **and symbol of democratic resistance against authoritarianism in Venezuela, emphasizing "ballots over bullets" and leading the opposition.
 
• Praised for her courage despite life-threatening risks and for unifying the opposition around democratic principles.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Distribution:**

 
 
• United States leads with six laureates.
 
• Other countries: Japan (2 laureates), Australia, Hungary, and Venezuela (1 laureate each).
 
 
 
• **Ceremony:** 
 
 
• The award ceremony will take place on December 10, 2025, in Stockholm (Peace Prize in Oslo).
 
• Each prize includes 11 million Swedish kronor, a gold medal, and a diploma.
